original_value: AbstractThis paper aims to understand the uses of technology in the informal recycling sector. We investigated the case of Relix, in northeast Brazil. The Relix project consists of cultural and educational interventions that promote recyclable waste picking and provides a mobile application to connect the local population to waste pickers. Methodological procedures included semistructured interviews with different groups of stakeholders. We adopted the Multilevel and pluralistic conceptual framework to analyze the groups according to the use of technology and perceptions in which they live based on context, process, and content. Results demonstrate that although the mobile application (app) can help waste pickers and the population to connect, it cannot single‐handedly promote any meaningful changes in the lives of people. Additional actions should be taken. This study has two important contributions. First, it describes how the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) can improve working conditions and create more innovative and equitable environments. Second, it enriches the theoretical discussion on the use of technology in social practice and the advances of applying a theoretical framework in the context of informal recycling.

result.paraphrase: This paper examines how technology is used in the informal recycling sector through the Relix case in northeast Brazil. The Relix project combines cultural and educational interventions that encourage recyclable waste picking and offers a mobile app linking local residents with waste pickers. To conduct the study, we used semistructured interviews with several stakeholder groups and analyzed them through the Multilevel and pluralistic conceptual framework, considering context, process, and content alongside participants’ technology use and perceptions. The findings show that, while the app can help connect waste pickers and the public, it cannot by itself bring about meaningful changes in people’s lives; further actions are needed. The study makes two key contributions: it shows how Information and Communication Technology (ICT) can improve working conditions and foster more innovative and equitable environments, and it deepens the theoretical discussion of technology use in social practice while advancing the application of a theoretical framework in informal recycling.
